options.A: Atypical squamous cells with varying degrees of mitotic activity
options.C: Nonspecific inflammatory features with C. trachomatis amplification on PCR
options.D: Safety pin-shaped intracellular inclusions that appear purple on Giemsa stain

full_context: A 58-year-old male presents to his primary care physician complaining of a painless bump on his penis. He first noticed the lesion 1 year ago but was too embarrassed to mention the issue at his last annual physical exam. The lesion has since grown in size and has recently become more erythematous. He has hypertension treated with lisinopril. At age 45, he was successfully treated for phimosis with a steroid cream. He first engaged in sexual intercourse at age 14 and has had “too many sexual partners to count” in his lifetime. He smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years but quit 10 years ago. He drinks one alcoholic beverage daily. Physical examination shows a nontender 5 mm x 5 mm ulcerated lesion with an erythematous base on the dorsum of the glans. There is no inguinal lymphadenopathy. Excisional biopsy of the lesion is performed.
